children: CEO Sam Altman said on X that frontier AI development needs to be paced and not stopped.
Altman’s statement is the latest in public comments made by AI majors over the past few days regarding AI safety and responsible development.
In the face of potential risks, Anthropic
CEO Dario Amodei said on the weekend that the progress of improving AI model capabilities should be slowed down.

“We welcome a federal framework that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI. But we do not believe we need to wait for an antitrust exemption or legislation to begin the work of providing this confidence,” Altman said, reinforcing the idea of self-regulating AI development.
House Speaker Mike Johnson said Congress should consult the leaders of Anthropic (
), formerly known as xAI, for a major meeting before Congress moves ahead with AI regulations.
Altman highlighted OpenAI’s formulation of safety cases ahead of frontier AI learning runs, along with other safety work in advance of model releases.

“When we talk about 'pacing,' we do not mean 'stopping.' Progress has been rapid and will continue to be. But it should be slower than it otherwise could be; interventions like safety cases and monitoring have significant costs,” the executive noted.

Altman highlighted two adverse pathways to irresponsible AI development, with the first being “loss of control of the future to AI” and the second being the concentration of AI capabilities into one person or company.
“Avoiding these two threats requires walking a narrow middle path; for example, one country could gain too much power. Another example is one lab ending up with too much power,” he said.

title: OpenAI CEO calls for ‘pacing, not stopping’ AI development
